title: cast_dim2flat

## Cast Dimensional List into a Flattened List {.unnumbered}


### Description

<code>cast_dim2flat()</code> casts a dimensional list
(i.e. recursive array)
into a flat list
(i.e. recursive vector),
but with names that indicate the original dimensional positions of the elements. <br />
<br />
Primary purpose for this function
is to facilitate printing or summarizing dimensional lists. <br />
<br />



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>cast_dim2flat(x, ...)

## Default S3 method:
cast_dim2flat(x, ...)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="x">x</code></td>
<td>
a list
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="...">...</code></td>
<td>
further arguments passed to or from methods. <br /> <br />
</td></tr>
</table>


### Value

A flattened list,
with names that indicate the original dimensional positions of the elements. <br />
<br />



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = NA}
library("broadcast")


# ideal scenario ====
x <- list(
  group1 = list(
    id1 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    ),
    id2 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    ),
    id3 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    )
  ),
  group2 = list(
    id1 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    ),
    id2 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    ),
    id3 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    )
  )
)

print(x)

hier2dim(x) # predict what dimensions `x` would have if casted as dimensional
x2 <- cast_hier2dim(x) # cast as dimensional

# since the original list uses the same names for all elements within the same depth,
# dimnames can be set easily:
dimnames(x2) <- list(
  names( x[[1]][[1]] ),
  names( x[[1]] ),
  names( x )
)
print(x2) # very compact, maybe too compact...?

# print a small portion of the list, but less compact:
cast_dim2flat(x2[, 1:2, "group1", drop = FALSE])




```
